title: Streamed text cut off by the output token limit
summary: The model stops at the output token limit in the middle of a streamed plain-text answer.

messages.content: Write a 200-word paragraph about the history of Kyiv, in English.

requirements.text: The caller can tell that the stream stopped at the token limit.
The streamed text is reported exactly as the provider sent it.
Output token usage is reported, and matches the provider's count.

grading_notes: The finish comes in the last event before the stream ends, so a library that only passes the text on can't satisfy the first requirement; a finish reason of length or a dedicated truncation error does. openai-chat sends no usage in this stream, because the call doesn't set stream_options.include_usage, so its truth has no usage for the second requirement to compare; the form with include_usage is planned as a scenario of its own, truncation.text-stream-usage. Effort none keeps the 16-token limit from being spent on reasoning.
